When the answer was to the whole Bill and interroga
before, it was exceptionable if every part was not com-
pletely answered. The exceptions were argued before
the Master, and, if they were allowed, the Defendant was
compelled to file a further answer. This practice is now
of course abolished, or it would clash with the 28th
New Order. The 30th New Order provides : :—
